metadata.title: feat: Phase 2.4 Features — Pagefind inline search + visible RSS link (GoatCounter deferred)

decisions.text: Pagefind UI pattern is an inline <input> field embedded in the header (same row as menu/lang-switcher/toggle), not a modal or a dedicated /search/ page. Uses the Pagefind UI default widget with CSS overrides to flatten it into an inline search input; results drop into an absolutely-positioned container under the input.

Pagefind runs as a post-Hugo step in the Netlify build pipeline (hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public). pagefind is added as a devDependency in package.json (new file) so Netlify caches it between builds. Local dev uses `hugo server` without Pagefind — search field renders disabled with a hint message when the /pagefind/ index is absent.

RSS link renders as a small ⚡ icon (lucide feed) inside the header menu, between the lang switcher and theme toggle. Per-language: PT points at /index.xml, EN points at /en/index.xml. Auto-generated by Hugo at /index.xml and /en/index.xml with no template work needed (PaperMod default).

GoatCounter integration is deferred out of Phase 2.4 at user request — the free-tier account is not yet created. Will be re-planned as a follow-up (Phase 2.4b or 2.5) once the owner has a goatcounter.com subdomain. The CSP scope decision (script-src https://marcelioleal.goatcounter.com) is recorded here so the follow-up phase does not re-litigate it.

When GoatCounter ships, CSP in static/_headers will use the domain-specific scope `script-src https://marcelioleal.goatcounter.com` (not the *.goatcounter.com wildcard). Follows principle of least privilege.

userStories.title: Wire Pagefind into Netlify build and ship the /pagefind/ static index
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want a Pagefind search index generated at build time so that every post and page is searchable on the live site without a backend or runtime dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json exists at the repo root and declares `pagefind` as a devDependency at a pinned minor version; `npm install` from a fresh checkout resolves without errors.

netlify.toml `[build]` command is updated from `hugo --minify` to `hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind`; a successful Netlify build produces `public/pagefind/pagefind.js`, `public/pagefind/pagefind-ui.js`, `public/pagefind/pagefind-ui.css`, and at least one `.pf_fragment` file.

A local invocation `hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind` exits 0 and writes files under `public/pagefind/`; the index covers at minimum content/pt-br/posts/** and content/en/posts/** (pagefind auto-crawls the built HTML).
README.md documents the new build sequence (Hugo then Pagefind) and notes that `hugo server` alone does not generate the index — local search testing requires the two-step build.
pagefind binary is pinned via package-lock.json committed to git so Netlify installs the same version deterministically.
userStories.notes: Pagefind is node-based (npx). Netlify's default Node version supports it out of the box. The devDependency approach lets Netlify's npm cache reuse it across builds — no global install needed. public/pagefind/ is under public/ which is already in .gitignore (Hugo output), so the index itself is not committed.

implementation.approach: Run `npm init -y` once, then `npm install --save-dev pagefind@latest` which writes both package.json (devDependencies.pagefind) and package-lock.json. Edit netlify.toml [build] command from `hugo --minify` to `hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind`. Document the two-step build in README.md so future-you remembers that `hugo server` dev mode does not include search. No layout work in this story — US-002 adds the UI.

verification.expect: Running `hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind` from the repo root exits 0 and produces public/pagefind/pagefind-ui.js plus pagefind-ui.css and at least one .pf_fragment file. The netlify.toml build command carries both steps chained with &&.

tasks: Run npm init -y to seed package.json with repo metadata
Run npm install --save-dev pagefind@latest to pin pagefind and generate package-lock.json
Edit netlify.toml [build] command from hugo --minify to hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind
Add a Pagefind section to README.md documenting the two-step local build and noting hugo server does not include search
Verify locally: rm -rf public && hugo --minify && npx pagefind --site public --output-subdir pagefind, then assert public/pagefind/pagefind-ui.js and pagefind-ui.css exist

userStories.title: Embed an inline Pagefind search field in the header
userStories.description: As a bilingual site visitor, I want a search input visible in the site header so that I can search the entire site from any page without clicking into a modal or a separate page.
acceptanceCriteria:
layouts/partials/header.html gains a `
` element inside the menu
    , placed between the lang switcher and the theme toggle.

layouts/partials/extend_head.html loads `/pagefind/pagefind-ui.js` and `/pagefind/pagefind-ui.css` with `defer` attributes, and includes an inline initialization snippet `new PagefindUI({ element: '#search', showImages: false, showSubResults: true })` inside a DOMContentLoaded handler.

When the /pagefind/ index is absent (local `hugo server`), the header input renders in a disabled state with placeholder text `Buscar... (apenas em produção)` for PT and `Search... (production only)` for EN — no console error leaks to visitors.

assets/css/extended/custom.css contains `.pm-search` overrides that flatten the Pagefind UI default widget into an inline input 180px wide (max), bg transparent with 1px border-var(--border), monospace font 13px, that expands to 240px on focus. On mobile (< 900px) the input collapses to an icon-only trigger that expands inline on tap.
Both PT home (public/index.html) and EN home (public/en/index.html) include the search div in the rendered header. Typing in production returns Pagefind results ranked across posts and pages.
userStories.notes: Pagefind UI's default widget is quite styled; a CSS reset on .pm-search is needed to flatten it. The i18n strings for the placeholder live in i18n/pt-br.yaml and i18n/en.yaml as `search_placeholder` and `search_placeholder_disabled`.

userStories.title: Expose per-language RSS feed link in the header
userStories.description: As a visitor who follows blogs via feed reader, I want a visible RSS link in the header so that I can subscribe to new posts in my own language without hunting through the source.
acceptanceCriteria: layouts/partials/header.html gains an <li> inside the menu <ul> containing an <a> with href="{{ "index.xml" | relLangURL }}" so the link resolves to /index.xml on PT pages and /en/index.xml on EN pages.

The anchor contains an inline SVG feed icon (Lucide 'rss' or equivalent 18×18 single-path SVG) and an aria-label with the i18n string `rss_aria_label` (PT: `Feed RSS`, EN: `RSS feed`). No visible text label — icon-only, consistent with the theme-toggle button style.

Both /index.xml and /en/index.xml exist in the Hugo build output (they are auto-generated by PaperMod — no template work needed) and validate as RSS 2.0 (<rss version="2.0"> root, with <channel><title>, <link>, <item>s).
The RSS icon sits between the lang switcher and the search input (or theme toggle on mobile) in the rendered menu. Hover state: color shifts to var(--accent) matching the other menu-item hover.
Rendered HTML for both PT home and EN home contains <a href="/index.xml"> and <a href="/en/index.xml"> respectively, both marked with rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml".
userStories.notes: Hugo's RSS output is enabled by default in PaperMod. No hugo.toml change needed. The rel="alternate" + type="application/rss+xml" attributes let feed readers auto-detect.

implementation.approach: Add an <li> inside #menu with an <a href="{{ "index.xml" | relLangURL }}" rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" aria-label="{{ i18n "rss_aria_label" }}"> containing an inline 18×18 feed SVG with stroke="currentColor". Add .header-rss class CSS to match the theme-toggle sizing and hover state.

verification.expect: After hugo --minify, curl http://localhost:1314/ returns HTML containing `<a href="/index.xml" rel="alternate"` and curl http://localhost:1314/en/ returns the same anchor pointing at /en/index.xml. Fetching /index.xml returns valid RSS 2.0 XML.

tasks: Add rss_aria_label i18n strings to pt-br.yaml (Feed RSS) and en.yaml (RSS feed)
Add an <li class="header-rss"> with the RSS anchor + inline feed SVG to layouts/partials/header.html, between the lang switcher and the theme-toggle <li>
Use href="{{ "index.xml" | relLangURL }}" so Hugo resolves per-language
Add .header-rss CSS matching theme-toggle size + hover color in custom.css
Build and curl PT and EN homes to confirm both RSS anchors render with correct per-language hrefs
curl /index.xml and /en/index.xml to confirm both return <rss version="2.0"> XML

userStories.title: Exit verify: Pagefind returns ranked results on staging and RSS validates
userStories.description: As the phase gatekeeper, I want an end-to-end verification on the deployed Netlify staging that Pagefind search works and both RSS feeds validate, so that Phase 2.4 can be marked completed on the roadmap.
acceptanceCriteria: After the Netlify deploy following the Phase 2.4 push completes successfully (deploy log shows both `hugo --minify` and `pagefind --site public` steps exited 0), browsing new.marcelioleal.com shows the search input in the header on both PT and EN.
Typing a query known to exist in the corpus (e.g. 'kite', 'nubank', 'burning man') in the header search returns at least 3 ranked results from the Pagefind dropdown within 500ms of keyup.
`curl -I https://new.marcelioleal.com/index.xml` returns 200 OK with Content-Type `application/rss+xml` (or `application/xml`), and the body parses as valid RSS 2.0 via `xmllint --noout`.
`curl -I https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/index.xml` returns the same, for the EN feed.
The RSS icon anchor in the header carries hreflang-correct target: the PT home's icon links to /index.xml, the EN home's icon links to /en/index.xml.

handoff.md is authored under .aimi/tasks/wordpress-to-hugo-migration/phase-2.4-features-search-rss-analytics/handoff.md recording: Pagefind index size, number of indexed documents, RSS validation output, and the GoatCounter deferral rationale for the follow-up phase.
roadmap.json entry for phase 2.4 is marked status=completed via aimi-cli roadmap-mark-complete; the aimi-cli also materializes the `creates` identities (pagefind_index) as verified.
userStories.notes: This story is the gate. Only runs after the first three stories are shipped and pushed to main. The GoatCounter line in the handoff is the handoff to the future follow-up phase — it should name the exact i18n strings, CSP scope, and extend_head.html placement that were pre-decided here.

implementation.approach: Wait for the Netlify deploy after the Phase 2.4 push; run the five curl/browser checks against new.marcelioleal.com. Author the handoff.md documenting what shipped, Pagefind corpus size, and the GoatCounter deferral. Then run aimi-cli roadmap-mark-complete for phase 2.4 with the evidence.

verification.expect: Live staging shows the search field in the header, returns ranked Pagefind results for a known query, and both /index.xml and /en/index.xml return valid RSS 2.0.
